newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Fierce Israeli-Palestinian clashes in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Fierce Israeli-Palestinian clashes in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian protesters, shouting the name of a Moslem suicide bomber, threw petrol bombs and rocks at Israeli soldiers who responded with rubber bullets and teargas in fierce clashes on Saturday in the West Bank town of Hebron.

Hospital officials said at least 20 Arabs were wounded by rubber-coated metal bullets and that one Palestinian lost an eye in the second day of battles along a confrontation line dividing the Palestinian and Israeli-controlled sections of the city.
Dozens of Palestinians were treated for teargas inhalation.
The Israeli army said four soldiers were lightly injured by rocks.

Tension has been high since Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in occupied West Bank.

On Friday, a Moslem suicide bomber identified by Palestinian sources as Mousa Abdel-Qader Ghneimat killed three Israeli women in an attack on a Tel Aviv cafe. The militant Hamas group claimed responsibility.

Shouting "With souls and blood we will sacrifice ourselves for you, Mousa", hundreds of Arab youths swept past Palestinian police and hurled petrol bombs and rocks at Israeli soldiers on several Hebron streets, witnesses said.
Protesters also burned an Israeli flag.
Order was briefly restored with the arrival at the scene of Jibril Rajoub, the PLO security chief in the West Bank, with Palestinian police reinforcements.
But hundreds of Palestinian students then flocked to the line and began throwing stones at Israeli troops, witnesses said.
On one street, Israeli soldiers stood alongside Palestinian policemen to face the protesters.
"Additional Israeli forces were sent to the city along with a message to Palestinian security officials that they must prevent unrest in areas under their control," an Israeli military source said.

The clashes were as heavy as those on Friday when at least 13 Arab youths were wounded by rubber bullets and dozens were treated for teargas inhalation in the most serious unrest since Israel handed most of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January.
The Israeli army declared a curfew on Friday on the Israeli-controlled section of Hebron where 400 Jewish settlers guarded by the army live among thousands of Palestinians.
An army spokesman said the curfew barred Palestinians, not Israelis, from moving around in the area.
